Boston, Massachusetts, is one of 11 U.S. cities hosting matches this summer(Image: Getty)

As the start of the 2026 World Cup nears, visitors from all over the world may be experiencing certain U.S. cities for the first time.

Boston, Massachusetts, is one of 11 U.S. cities hosting matches this summer, and the Northeast city is expecting to welcome over 3 million international fans to the city. Boston Stadium, also known as Gillette Stadium, will host seven matches for the FIFA World Cup 2026.

Though avid fans will be there for the matches, they may also want to check out one of the U.S.’ oldest cities while they’re in town. Here’s a guide on what to do while in Boston for the 2026 World Cup:

Boston is home to a variety of activities, from historical sites and museums to acclaimed restaurants. It’s a great place for American history buffs, who can see several major locations that were instrumental in the founding of the country.

The 2.5-mile Freedom Trail passes through 16 historical locations throughout the city

On that note, the best place to start is with the Freedom Trail. The 2.5-mile trail passes through 16 historical locations throughout the city. Visitors can sign up for a tour with a guide explaining the significance, or they can do the trail themselves at their own pace. Audio guides are also available, and it takes about two to three hours to complete.

The Freedom Trail begins in downtown Boston, crosses through the North End, and finishes at the Bunker Hill Monument in Charlestown. Trekkers will see Faneuil Hall, the Paul Revere House, and the USS Constitution frigate, also known as Old Ironsides.

Founded in 1912, Fenway Park is the oldest active baseball stadium in the U.S.

While soccer is the main sport on visitors’ minds, it wouldn’t be a trip to Boston without visiting Fenway Park. Founded in 1912, it’s the oldest active baseball stadium in the U.S. and home to the Boston Red Sox.

Fans can catch a game at the park or take a guided tour, getting a peek around the locker rooms and other areas that are usually off limits.

The Boston Tea Party Ships and Museum allows visitors to take a step back in time to experience the beginning of the American Revolution for themselves

Perhaps one of Boston’s most well-known historical events, the Boston Tea Party Ships and Museum allows visitors to take a step back in time to experience the beginning of the American Revolution for themselves.

The museum includes live reenactments with actors, interactive exhibits and full-scale replicas of the 18th century ships. It even allows guests to take part in tossing the tea into the harbor.

Boston Common is the oldest public park in the city

For a free destination in the city, guests should check out Boston Public Garden in the heart of the city near Boston Common. Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, who’s also behind New York City’s Central Park, Boston Public Garden has over 600 varieties of trees and various beautiful flower displays.

Boston Common is right next door, and it’s the oldest public park in the city. It’s the perfect place to bring a blanket and spend a few hours enjoying nature and people watching.

You can make a stop at Quincy Market as you progress along the Freedom Trail

You can make a stop at Quincy Market as you progress along the Freedom Trail. The historic market was established in 1826, and it has over a hundred vendors, restaurants and food courts to enjoy.

Visitors can learn a bit about the building’s history or pick up some Boston favorites, like lobster rolls or clam chowder.
